question.:question/problem: Calculate ${f}^{′}(x)$ if $f(x)=5{e}^{2x}+8.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=5{e}^{u}+8,\,u=2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=5{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =5{e}^{u}\cdot 2 \\  & =10{e}^{u} \\  & =10{e}^{2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=1/6} & ={(30{e}^{6x})|}_{x=1/6} \\  & =30{e}^{6(1/6)} \\  & =30e\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={(5{e}^{6x})|}_{x=1/6} \\  & =5{e}^{6(1/6)} \\  & =5e.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5e & =30e(x-\frac{1}{6}) \\ y-5e & =30ex-5e \\ y & =30ex\end{aligned}
$$
